status: synthetic AI-authored reference, not validated linguistic truth
limitations: Span and category agreement cannot establish that feedback is pedagogically correct.
Review every question and hint for leading answers, false accusations, age appropriateness, disagreement bias and invented facts.
Coverage is a targeted acceptance set, not representative performance or exam calibration.
Version 2 adds candidate challenge/revision cases; the difficulty labels are preferences, not calibrated text difficulty.

cases.prompt: How do students in your town get to school?
cases.text: Every morning my sister walk to school with her friends. She say the road is safe, but the traffic near the market are heavy. My parents worries about her. The school bus come at seven, but it is always full. I think the town need a new bus route for students. Then everyone could reach school safely and on time.

annotations.note: Singular subject needs walks.
She needs says.

annotations.quote: the traffic near the market are
annotations.note: The singular subject traffic requires is, not are. This does not by itself identify the cause of the error.
Plural subject needs worry.
Singular subject needs comes.
Singular subject needs needs.

protected.quote: everyone could reach school safely
protected.why: Correct modal use.

cases.prompt: Should our school have a reading hour?
cases.text: Our school should have a reading hour because having a reading hour is a good idea. It would be the right thing for our school to do. That is why I think our school should introduce it.

annotations.quote: because having a reading hour is a good idea.

cases.prompt: Should all shops extend their opening hours?

annotations.quote: Therefore every shop in the city should stay open later
annotations.note: One instance does not establish universal causal benefit.

cases.prompt: Should a company introduce free delivery?
cases.text: The company should offer free delivery because it will increase profits by exactly forty percent. I have not examined any sales or cost information. The increase is certain, so there is no need to test the policy before adopting it.

cases.prompt: Should a library remain open later?

protected.quote: Staff costs are a reasonable objection, so the trial should record attendance and costs before any longer commitment is made.
protected.why: The draft explicitly considers the strongest stated cost objection; do not claim it is absent.

cases.prompt: Write a formal report of your class tree-planting activity, using complete sentences and standard sentence boundaries.
cases.text: Our class planted trees last week it was hard work. Some students dug the holes, others carried water. Because the soil was dry. We used a lot of water. The teacher was pleased, she said the trees would grow quickly. Next month we will plant flowers near the gate.

annotations.quote: Our class planted trees last week it was hard work
annotations.note: Two sentences fused without punctuation.

annotations.quote: Some students dug the holes, others carried water
annotations.note: A separator or conjunction may help in this formal report, but short balanced coordination can be rhetorical. Do not require this as a diagnosed grammar error.
A subordinate clause on its own is a fragment.

annotations.note: Comma splice.

protected.quote: Next month we will plant flowers near the gate.
protected.why: Correct sentence.

cases.prompt: Should mobile phones be allowed in school?
cases.text: Mobile phones should be allowed in school. However, they help students find information quickly. Some students play games in class. Therefore, phones can be useful in an emergency. In conclusion, schools should make clear rules.

annotations.note: However signals contrast, but this sentence supports the claim.
Therefore signals a result that does not follow from the previous sentence.

annotations.quote: Some students play games in class.
annotations.note: A transition could help signal this counterpoint, but the complete sentence is not a grammatical error.

protected.quote: In conclusion, schools should make clear rules.
protected.why: Appropriate concluding connective.

protected.quote: Some students play games in class.
protected.why: A complete counterpoint need not always carry an explicit connective; a style suggestion is permitted.

cases.prompt: Explain what a committee should check before deciding whether to expand a service.
cases.text: The committee requested several informations before deciding whether to expand the service. A limited pilot could reveal costs that the original proposal overlooked, although the results would need to be interpreted cautiously if the pilot location differed from the other branches.

annotations.note: Information is uncountable here; several pieces of information or more information would fit.
The preposition in this construction is on: depends on.

cases.prompt: State one consistent recommendation about a permanent ban on cars in the town centre.
cases.text: I support a permanent ban on every private car in the town centre, without exceptions. At the same time, I oppose any ban on private cars there, without exceptions. These are both my final recommendation. The council should follow my recommendation when it makes its decision.

annotations.quote: These are both my final recommendation.
annotations.note: The draft presents mutually incompatible recommendations without resolving or qualifying them.
acceptQuotes: I support a permanent ban on every private car in the town centre, without exceptions.
At the same time, I oppose any ban on private cars there, without exceptions.

cases.prompt: Explain which school group should make a decision and why.
cases.text: The reading club asked the sports club to share its room after school. They said they should decide because it belongs to them. I agree with their decision, but I have not named which club I mean. This would settle the disagreement fairly.

annotations.quote: They said they should decide because it belongs to them.
annotations.note: The reader cannot identify which club the pronouns refer to; ask the writer to name it.

cases.prompt: Make a case for longer school library hours, fairly addressing the objection that staffing them may be too expensive.
cases.text: Our school should extend library hours so students have more time to read. People who question the staffing cost do not deserve an answer. They simply hate books and want children to fail. This proves that their objection is wrong and that the school should ignore it.

annotations.quote: They simply hate books and want children to fail.
annotations.note: The response misrepresents a stated cost objection instead of addressing it; do not supply the rebuttal.

cases.prompt: Write a focused argument about whether a council should fund a bus route, keeping the paragraphs relevant to the recommendation.
cases.text:
The council should trial a bus route between the estate and the hospital because some residents cannot make that journey by public transport.

My favourite film has a detective who wears a blue coat. The soundtrack is exciting and the ending surprised me.

The trial should record usage and cost before the council decides whether to continue the route.

annotations.quote: My favourite film has a detective who wears a blue coat.
annotations.note: The middle paragraph interrupts the route from problem to trial with unrelated material; ask about its purpose.

cases.prompt: Revise your expansion recommendation to acknowledge what one profitable branch can and cannot show.
cases.text: The company could test expansion in one additional branch before committing more money. One profitable branch does not establish that every location will perform similarly. The trial should examine local demand and costs, and the company should reconsider expansion if the expected benefit does not materialise.

protected.quote: One profitable branch does not establish that every location will perform similarly.
protected.why: The current draft explicitly rejects universal generalisation. Do not repeat the earlier resolved concern or claim improvement/mastery.

cases.previous: The company should expand immediately because one branch made a profit. This proves that every branch will make the same profit. No differences between branches matter, and we do not need to investigate any further before committing the money.

cases.prompt: Revise the proposal by checking what your evidence supports.
cases.text: The council should build a playground because every resident wants one. I still have not asked any residents about their views. I have added a sentence about maintenance costs, but that does not provide evidence about how many residents support the proposal.

annotations.note: The universal support claim remains unsupported in the current draft, despite other changes.

cases.previous: The council should build a playground because every resident wants one. I have not asked any residents about their views. I think the council should act immediately, and there is no need to discuss access or maintenance before it starts building.

cases.prompt: Make a qualified case against judging public services only by their easily measured outputs.
cases.text: Public services should not be judged solely by easily measured outputs. A clinic can count appointments without showing whether patients received useful care. Outcome measures are also imperfect, since causes may be difficult to separate, but combining several indicators with contextual review would be more informative than treating one activity count as a complete measure of value.

protected.quote: Outcome measures are also imperfect, since causes may be difficult to separate
protected.why: The writer acknowledges a limitation in the preferred alternative; do not call the argument wholly one-sided.

protected.quote: Public services should not be judged solely by easily measured outputs.
protected.why: The qualified position answers the assigned against task.

cases.prompt: Revise the library proposal in your own words.
cases.text: The school could open its library for one extra afternoon each week so students have a quiet place to read. A short trial would show how many students use it. Staff availability would need to be checked before the school promises to continue.

protected.quote: A short trial would show how many students use it.
protected.why: The proposal is to collect evidence rather than falsely claim that usage has already been measured.
